reviewed_by: claude-opus-5 blind reviewer, re-review after the triangle-validity and shape-variation fixes, 2026-08-13

samples_reviewed.question_text: A triangle has sides 2 cm, 1 cm, and 2 cm. What is its perimeter?
A rectangle has sides 5 cm and 12 cm. What is its perimeter?
A square has a side of 9 cm. What is its perimeter?
A square has a side of 7 cm. What is its perimeter?
A rectangle has sides 7 cm and 1 cm. What is its perimeter?
A square has a side of 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
A square has a side of 17 cm. What is its perimeter?
A triangle has sides 10 cm, 21 cm, and 17 cm. What is its perimeter?
A triangle has sides 12 cm, 6 cm, and 17 cm. What is its perimeter?
A square has a side of 6 cm. What is its perimeter?

A rectangle has sides 7 cm and 3 cm. What is its perimeter?
A square has a side of 3 cm. What is its perimeter?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: All fifteen samples ask for exactly what the sentence names, the perimeter of a triangle, square or rectangle, and every answer checks out: seed 501 'A triangle has sides 10 cm, 21 cm, and 17 cm. What is its perimeter?' gives 48, seed 500 'A square has a side of 17 cm. What is its perimeter?' gives 68, seed 602 'A rectangle has sides 7 cm and 3 cm. What is its perimeter?' gives 20. Every item is answerable from the numbers in its own stem, with no missing side and no second unknown.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All three shapes the sentence names appear separately. Triangles at seeds 42, 501, 502 and 604; squares at seeds 44, 45, 50, 500, 600 and 603; rectangles at seeds 43, 46, 602 and 605, with seed 601 'A rectangular garden is 11 cm long and 10 cm wide.' adding a rectangle in context. Every triangle described can actually exist under the triangle inequality: seed 42 'A triangle has sides 2 cm, 1 cm, and 2 cm. What is its perimeter?' has 1+2>2, seed 604 has 2+4>4, seed 501 has 10+17>21, and the tightest case, seed 502 'A triangle has sides 12 cm, 6 cm, and 17 cm. What is its perimeter?', has 6+12=18>17, so all four are constructible.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Each item is one addition or one doubling on whole centimetres, with the largest answer 68 at seed 500 'A square has a side of 17 cm. What is its perimeter?' and most well under 40, comfortably inside grade 2 addition. Nothing requires a formula, a missing side, unit conversion, or a second step; seed 50 'A square has a side of 5 cm. What is its perimeter?' is representative of the load.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Two formatters are exercised (mcq at seed 602, cloze at seeds 50, 500, 601 and 605), all three shapes recur with varied side values from 1 up to 21, isosceles and scalene triangles both appear (seed 604 'A triangle has sides 2 cm, 4 cm, and 4 cm. What is its perimeter?' against seed 502), and seed 601 supplies a contextual framing with 'How much fencing is needed to go all the way around it?' alongside the bare geometric stems. The template is uniform, which suits a find-the-perimeter competency, and the variation lands on the shapes and values that matter here.

competency_alignment.rationale: Nothing reaches past the sentence and nothing falls short of it. No sample asks for area, for a missing side given the perimeter, or for a shape outside the three named; no sample stops at measuring a single length. Seed 605 'A rectangle has sides 10 cm and 7 cm. What is its perimeter?' is the pattern throughout, and the one contextual item, seed 601, still asks only for the distance around a rectangle.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The bare geometric stems are fine, since a drawn triangle or square of 3 to 21 cm is exactly what a grade 2 ruler handles. The single item that names a real object gets the unit wrong: seed 601 'A rectangular garden is 11 cm long and 10 cm wide.' describes a garden about the size of a postcard, roughly two orders of magnitude too small, when 11 m by 10 m is the plausible reading. The arithmetic and the answer 42 are correct; only the object-to-unit pairing is implausible, and it is the only contextual item in the pool, so the one bad case is also the whole context sample.
